documents: Passport (notarised copy if by post), proof of foreign address, existing-bank reference letter, foreign TIN or Jamaican TRN, source of funds.
min_deposit_fees: Scotiabank Jamaica lists minimum opening balances of about 100 for foreign-currency savings up to JMD 5,000-10,000 for chequing/savings; monthly fees vary by account.
banks: National Commercial Bank (NCB), Scotiabank Jamaica.
restrictions: NCB requires non-residents to open in person at a branch; enhanced KYC and FATCA/CRS reporting apply; USD accounts available.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for JMD transfers; remittance services; no local fintech accounts for non-residents.
cost_note: Scotiabank Jamaica JMD chequing/savings minimum opening balance JMD 5,000-10,000 (lower bound used, about USD 31 at JMD 160/USD; USD foreign-currency savings minimum is USD 100); a current opening fee and monthly fee for these accounts were not found in a published tariff (older 2016 brochure showed JMD 0-600/month), so those are null.

documents: Passport, second ID, proof of foreign address (utility bill), bank reference, source-of-funds evidence.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: National Bank of Dominica (case-by-case); other onshore banks not confirmed.
restrictions: Enhanced due diligence for non-residents and CBI-linked clients; EC dollar pegged to USD at 2.70; correspondent-banking de-risking in the Eastern Caribbean limits USD services.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut transfers; offshore banks under the Financial Services Unit; regional banks in other ECCU states.
cost_note: National Bank of Dominica handles non-residents case-by-case and publishes no non-resident opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee, so all three are null.

documents: Passport with entry stamp, proof of foreign address, source-of-funds documents, sometimes a bank reference; full accounts usually need a DIMEX residence card.
min_deposit_fees: Simplified non-resident accounts typically capped around USD 1,200-2,000 in monthly deposits; opening deposit and fees not published.
banks: Banco de Costa Rica (BCR) offers limited non-resident accounts; private banks such as BAC Credomatic case-by-case.
restrictions: Non-resident accounts carry monthly deposit caps and limited products; strict AML/KYC under SUGEF; branch acceptance is inconsistent.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for CRC transfers; keep funds in a home-country account.
cost_note: Banco de Costa Rica simplified non-resident accounts cap monthly deposits at about USD 1,200-2,000, but no opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee is published, so all three are null.

documents: Passport, CPF tax number (obtainable from abroad via consulate/Receita Federal), proof of foreign address, foreign TIN, source of funds.
min_deposit_fees: Non-resident (CNR) account fees are high at premium banks, e.g. one guide quotes BTG Pactual at about BRL 24,000 a year; others not published.
banks: Exchange-authorised banks offering the Conta de Nao Residente (CNR), e.g. BTG Pactual; mainstream retail banks rarely open for non-residents.
restrictions: Non-residents must use the CNR regime regulated by Banco Central do Brasil; retail banks generally require a residence permit (CRNM); annual CPF re-registration reported for non-residents.
alternatives: Wise (PIX-enabled transfers), Nomad or similar USD accounts for Brazilians; law-firm assisted remote onboarding.
cost_note: BTG Pactual non-resident (CNR) account reportedly costs about BRL 24,000 a year (BRL 2,000/month, about USD 370 at BRL 5.4/USD) per a third-party guide; opening fee and minimum deposit are not published, so null.

documents: Passport plus secondary ID, a Taiwan Record of ID Number or UBN from the National Immigration Agency, local address and phone; most banks require an ARC.
min_deposit_fees: Small NTD opening deposits typical (often around NTD 1,000); non-resident fees not published.
banks: none known that routinely accept non-residents; some private banks open passport-only accounts at branch discretion.
restrictions: FSC rules treat the ARC as the key ID; without it acceptance is at bank discretion and accounts may be restricted to limited functions; foreign-currency accounts and FX limits apply.
alternatives: Wise for TWD transfers; keep home-country account; offshore banking units (OBU) for some foreign clients.
cost_note: Typical small NTD opening deposit of about TWD 1,000 (about USD 32 at TWD 31/USD) at banks that accept passport-only clients at branch discretion; opening and monthly fees for non-residents are not published, so null.

documents: Passport (valid 3+ months), passport photo, proof of foreign address; branch openings usually want a long-term visa extension and lease; remote ACLEDA forms must be notarised and embassy-certified or confirmed by SWIFT MT999.
min_deposit_fees: ABA reported at about USD 50 for non-residents; ACLEDA current accounts about USD 1,000; fees low.
banks: ACLEDA Bank (overseas account opening), ABA Bank and Canadia Bank (in-branch with visa).
restrictions: Most banks require a valid stay extension; USD widely used; remote-opened accounts may be limited to email/phone banking until a local SIM is obtained.
alternatives: Wise for transfers; Bakong/KHQR wallets need local accounts; Wing and other mobile money mainly for residents.
cost_note: ACLEDA Bank standard savings account lists no opening fee, no initial deposit, no minimum balance and no monthly fee (USD-denominated; statements beyond two months cost USD 2/month), though ABA reportedly asks non-residents for about USD 50 and ACLEDA current accounts about USD 1,000.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, bank reference and source of funds; in-person branch visit.
min_deposit_fees: ANZ Samoa foreign-currency accounts for non-residents require a minimum of 200 units (e.g. AUD 200 or USD 200); fees not published.
banks: ANZ Samoa (foreign-currency accounts for non-resident individuals), BSP Samoa (case-by-case).
restrictions: Exchange controls administered by the Central Bank of Samoa; non-resident offerings are mainly foreign-currency accounts; tala accounts may be restricted.
alternatives: Wise or remittance services for WST; Digicel/Vodafone mobile money for residents.
cost_note: ANZ Samoa foreign-currency account for non-resident individuals requires a minimum of 200 units (USD 200 used; AUD 200 would be about USD 132 at AUD 1 = USD 0.66); opening and monthly fees are not published, so null.

documents: Passport (translated/notarised if needed), Turkish tax number (vergi numarasi, obtainable from abroad or at a tax office), proof of address (home-country utility bill), Turkish phone number.
min_deposit_fees: not published; some non-resident routes reportedly require around USD 6,000 held for three months.
banks: Ziraat Bankasi, VakifBank, Garanti BBVA, QNB, HSBC Turkey and Kuveyt Turk reported to accept some non-residents, varying by branch.
restrictions: Many banks increasingly require a residence permit (ID number starting with 99) and have tightened foreigner onboarding; strict AML checks; lira volatility and FX deposit rules.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for TRY transfers; Papara-type e-money wallets mostly need Turkish ID.
cost_note: Some non-resident routes at Turkish banks reportedly require about USD 6,000 held for three months (reported, not from a bank tariff); opening and monthly fees for non-resident personal accounts are not published, so null.

documents: Passport with valid visa, in-person application; bank-specific forms.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for routine non-resident onboarding; a 2017 Central Bank of Iran directive allows commercial banks to open rial accounts for foreigners in person.
restrictions: Comprehensive US/EU/UN-related sanctions and FATF blacklist status; Iranian banks are cut off from SWIFT and international cards; Australian sanctions also apply; foreign cards do not work in Iran.
alternatives: Tourist prepaid debit cards (e.g. Mah Card/tourist cards) loaded with cash in Iran; cash USD/EUR; no access via Wise or Revolut.
cost_note: Iranian banks may open rial accounts for foreigners in person under a 2017 central bank directive, but no fees or minimum deposits are published and sanctions block routine use, so all three are null.

documents: Passport, passport-size photo, proof of address; source-of-funds information for foreign-currency accounts.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Bank of Kigali (personal current accounts open to non-Rwandans in RWF, USD, EUR, GBP and others); remote diaspora accounts are for Rwandans.
restrictions: KYC requires in-person verification at a branch for foreigners; National Bank of Rwanda AML rules apply.
alternatives: MTN MoMo and Airtel Money mobile money (need local SIM registration); Wise transfers to RWF.
cost_note: Bank of Kigali personal current accounts are open to non-Rwandans, but no opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee was found in a published tariff, so all three are null.

documents: Passport with signed non-resident declaration, NUIT tax number, income statement or work contract, reference letter from home bank; foreign documents notarised, legalised by Mozambican consulate and in Portuguese.
min_deposit_fees: First Capital Bank minimum deposit about MZN 1,000; others not published.
banks: Millennium bim (published non-resident document list); First Capital Bank case-by-case.
restrictions: Bank of Mozambique foreign-exchange controls; foreign-currency accounts require justification such as service contracts; documents must be in Portuguese.
alternatives: M-Pesa (Vodacom) and e-Mola mobile money with local SIM; Wise transfers not widely supported to MZN.
cost_note: First Capital Bank minimum deposit of about MZN 1,000 (about USD 16 at MZN 64/USD); opening and monthly fees at First Capital Bank and Millennium bim for non-residents are not published, so null.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, foreign TIN, source-of-funds evidence and reason for a Belgian account; online opening generally requires Belgian residence or itsme/eID.
min_deposit_fees: Basic banking service about EUR 1.60/month at BNP Paribas Fortis (EU residents only); non-resident current-account fees not published.
banks: BNP Paribas Fortis (non-resident clients handled at designated branches, case-by-case); other banks discretionary.
restrictions: Statutory basic-account right covers only EU legal residents and certain Belgians abroad; banks may refuse non-EU residents for AML reasons; CRS reporting.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut (Belgian/Lithuanian IBAN available to many non-residents), N26 for EEA residents.
cost_note: BNP Paribas Fortis basic banking service of about EUR 1.60/month applies to EU residents only, and non-resident current-account fees are not published, so all three are null.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, recent bank statements, home-country tax return, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence.
min_deposit_fees: Reported opening deposits range from EUR 0-5,000 at some banks, but non-resident offerings are often private banking with six-figure minimums; Creand reportedly charges about EUR 200 to open and EUR 220 per semester.
banks: Andbank, Creand Credit Andorra, MoraBanc, Vall Banc (non-resident accounts case-by-case).
restrictions: Strict AML and source-of-funds checks; CRS automatic exchange with Australia; accounts in EUR; onboarding takes weeks.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for EUR; Spanish or French banks nearby.
cost_note: Creand Credit Andorra reportedly charges about EUR 200 to open (about USD 232) and EUR 220 per semester (about EUR 37/month, about USD 43) at EUR 1 = USD 1.16; the minimum deposit for non-residents is not published (reported EUR 0-5,000, often six figures for private banking), so null.

documents: Passport (original and copy), proof of address, 6-12 months of bank statements, source of income, evidence of economic ties to Montenegro (e.g. property ownership).
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: CKB (Crnogorska Komercijalna Banka) and other banks case-by-case with proof of local ties.
restrictions: Banks require a strong basis such as property or business ties; some nationalities restricted; branch visit required; EUR-denominated.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for EUR; banks in neighbouring EU states.
cost_note: CKB and other Montenegrin banks consider non-residents case-by-case and publish no non-resident opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee, so all three are null.

documents: Certified passport copy, proof of foreign address (under 3 months), bank reference, CV, income and source-of-wealth documents, foreign TIN.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Eurobank Cyprus (non-residents case-by-case with enhanced checks); Bank of Cyprus generally prefers residence permit holders.
restrictions: Heavy post-2013 de-risking and enhanced due diligence for non-residents; CRS reporting; banks may require a clear Cyprus nexus.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for EUR; licensed EMIs based in Cyprus offering IBANs.
cost_note: Eurobank Cyprus and Bank of Cyprus publish no non-resident personal opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee, so all three are null.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, documents proving a connection to Estonia (property, employment, business, study), source-of-funds evidence; e-Residency card is not accepted as ID.
min_deposit_fees: not published for personal accounts; banks charge non-refundable review fees for non-resident business applicants (about EUR 300 at LHV/Swedbank).
banks: LHV Pank, Swedbank, SEB (only with demonstrable Estonian connection).
restrictions: Non-residents cannot be identified digitally at LHV; e-Residency alone is not a basis for an account; tightened AML after the Danske scandal; special rules for Russian/Belarusian citizens.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, Paysera and other EMIs offering EUR IBANs with remote onboarding.
cost_note: LHV, Swedbank and SEB publish no non-resident personal-account fees (the about EUR 300 review fee applies to non-resident business applicants only), so all three are null.

documents: Passport, proof of address, home-bank references, purpose of account and source-of-funds declaration; branch visit or lawyer with power of attorney.
min_deposit_fees: Byblos Bank fresh-money account minimum USD 1,000; other banks not published.
banks: Byblos Bank (fresh accounts); BLOM and Bank Audi reported to open fresh accounts case-by-case.
restrictions: Post-2019 banking crisis with informal capital controls on legacy deposits; only fresh-money accounts are freely usable; FATF grey-listing (2024) and correspondent de-risking; no legal bar on non-residents.
alternatives: Cash USD, Whish Money and OMT money transfer services; Wise not supported for LBP payouts.
cost_note: Byblos Bank fresh-money account minimum of USD 1,000 (USD-denominated, no conversion); opening and monthly fees are not published, so null.

documents: Passport with Yemeni residence/visa and local address; in-person only.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for non-residents.
restrictions: Civil conflict with a split Central Bank (Aden vs Sanaa), dual currency rates, cash liquidity shortages; US designations of the Houthis and sanctions on Sanaa-based banks; most foreign banks avoid correspondent relationships.
alternatives: Hawala and remittance agents (e.g. Al-Kuraimi exchange network); Western Union-type transfers; no fintech access.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts at Yemeni banks, so all three are null.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign residence, funding by transfer from abroad, per Moroccan Office des Changes rules for non-resident convertible-dirham accounts.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Moroccan banks with branches in Laayoune and Dakhla (e.g. Bank of Africa, Attijariwafa, Banque Populaire) under Moroccan regulation; no Sahrawi (SADR) banks.
restrictions: Disputed territory administered by Morocco; Moroccan exchange controls apply (non-resident convertible-dirham or foreign-currency accounts only); dirham not exportable; very limited banking outside main towns.
alternatives: Open a non-resident convertible-dirham account at a Moroccan bank in Rabat/Casablanca; Wise transfers to MAD.
cost_note: Moroccan banks with branches in Laayoune and Dakhla publish no non-resident personal-account fees or minimum deposits for this territory, so all three are null.

documents: Passport with valid Indian visa, proof of overseas address, photograph, PAN or Form 60, and in-person KYC at an authorised dealer bank branch in India.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: Authorised dealer banks may open NRO savings/current accounts for visiting foreign nationals of non-Indian origin under FEMA; few banks advertise this, and NRE/FCNR products are restricted to NRIs/OCIs.
restrictions: FEMA Deposit Regulations 2016 allow NRO deposits from persons resident outside India; for foreign visitors the account must be funded from abroad or by sale of foreign exchange brought in, and the balance is freely reconvertible on departure only if held 6 months or less with no local credits (otherwise RBI approval needed).
alternatives: UPI One World prepaid wallets for foreign visitors; Wise or Remitly transfers to INR.
cost_note: Authorised dealer banks may open NRO accounts for visiting foreign nationals of non-Indian origin, but no bank publishes fees or minimum balances for that route, so all three are null.

documents: Passport plus Non-Citizen Ghana Card (issued only to foreigners resident at least 90 days, needing a residence permit and in-person biometrics), proof of Ghana address, and work/employment documents where applicable.
min_deposit_fees: Reported 2026 tariffs: Societe Generale Ghana GHS 50 current account, OmniBSIC USD 50 FX current account, Stanbic GHS 500 opening and USD 5/month on FX accounts.
banks: none known for short-stay non-residents; Absa, Stanbic, GCB, Ecobank and Standard Chartered serve foreigners once they hold a Non-Citizen Ghana Card and residence permit.
restrictions: Bank of Ghana notice BG/GOV/SEC/2025/36 (effective 1 Dec 2025) reportedly bars financial transactions for customers without a Ghana Card or Non-Citizen Card, limiting visitors under 90 days to one-off transactions; FCA/FEA foreign-currency account rules apply.
alternatives: Wise or Remitly transfers to GHS; mobile money (MTN MoMo, Telecel Cash) requires a Ghana Card-registered SIM.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts without a Non-Citizen Ghana Card and residence permit, so all three are null (resident tariffs reported for 2026: Stanbic GHS 500 opening, about USD 45 at GHS 11/USD, and USD 5/month on FX accounts).

documents: Passport, proof of address, residence or work permit at most banks, Gambia TIN, and notarised ID for non-residents where accepted; branch visit required.
min_deposit_fees: not published (monthly maintenance reportedly around GMD 2-15).
banks: Ecobank Gambia reportedly considers non-residents with notarised ID, address proof and a Gambia TIN; Access Bank, GTBank and Trust Bank reportedly require residence/work permits or local ID.
restrictions: No remote non-resident onboarding found; standard KYC expects local ID and in-person visit; small market with limited correspondent banking and USD access.
alternatives: Wave and Afrimoney mobile money (local SIM needed); Western Union, MoneyGram and Wise transfers to GMD.
cost_note: Monthly maintenance at Gambian banks reportedly about GMD 2-15 (upper bound about USD 0.20 at GMD 72/USD), not from an Ecobank Gambia tariff; opening fee and minimum deposit are not published, so null.

documents: Photo ID (passport accepted) showing name, address and an identity number such as a CPR number, or residence/employment documents as substitutes, under Danish AML rules.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known; Gronlandsbanken and Bankivik (BankNordik's former Greenland site now redirects there) target local residents and newcomers and publish no non-resident personal offering.
restrictions: Danish krone and Danish FSA supervision; onboarding geared to CPR-registered residents, and accounts are blocked if ID requirements are not met; non-residents must contact banks case by case.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for DKK; a Danish bank account where eligible.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts at Gronlandsbanken or Bankivik, which serve local residents only, so all three are null.
